If you are married filing a joint return, the spouse who received the qualified tips must have a valid SSN." When that condition fails, Part II is not filled out, so line 12 is a skipped line (adjudication README: a nonzero amount on a line the source says to skip, on a reachable return, is a defect of the side producing it; the project encodes a skipped line as zero). The project prints line 12 only when Part II applies (s1a.part2); the candidate figures it on every return. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/s1a.deepseek.json; 1,083 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 111 partial records): 907 of 1694 comparisons agree; differences: 390 candidate-refuses, 259 value, 133 project-unknown, 3 project-refuses, 2 candidate-unknown; witnesses (project / candidate): candidate-refuses e.g. classm.w2.1.deepseek ($0.00 / refusal), classm.f8889.4.deepseek ($0.00 / refusal); value e.g. classm.f8889.2.deepseek ($0.00 / $8,400.00), classm.f4562.1 ($0.00 / $35,600.00); project-unknown e.g. classm.f4952.1 (unknown s1a.tips / $23,800.00), classm.f4952.2 (unknown s1a.tips / $34,800.00); project-refuses e.g. classm.retirement.3 (refusal / $0.00), classm.eic.4 (refusal / $0.00); candidate-unknown e.g. stage16.cleanup.refuse.f2441_line24 ($0.00 / unknown person[spouse].sav_trad), ss.mfs ($0.00 / unknown sb.unsupported). Host re-check of all 259 value records: s1a.part2 is false on every one. Reachable witness (full interview, canonical/2025/interview-full.json): 34 of the 107 interview-complete generated returns have s1a.part2 false and a nonzero candidate line 12, for example generated 20261026/5 (single; project $0.00 / candidate $60000.00). No later amount changes, because the candidate’s line 13 differences come from its ungated lines 4a and 4c and are ruled there, but under the README rule the nonzero skipped line is itself the defect. The unknown-kind records are not interview-producible: the full interview (canonical/2025/interview-full.json) reaches f1040.line13b = s1a.line38 on every return, and project lines 13, 21 and 30 read s1a.tips, s1a.overtime and s1a.carloan first, so those answers are always asked; the records lacking them are fixtures written for other forms (hundreds of unknown lines each) and partials that withhold them. Host re-check (read-only re-evaluation of the same bank, outside the triage record): every refusal-kind record, and every other unknown-kind record, is on a return that both runtimes refuse elsewhere (f1040.line11b and the sb, sd, eic, f2441 or s3.mfs refusals; married filing separately is refused for the whole return through s3.mfs in scope.yaml and s3.line11). The project-refuses records (for example classm.retirement.3, stage12.refuse.excluded_income) are refused by both runtimes at eic.step1_foreign. The candidate floors line 10 at zero instead of subtracting line 9 from line 8 again, which is the same amount.

The candidate drops the s1a.tips gate and the valid-SSN condition: it counts every person’s tip employers and sums every person’s person.tip_total. The candidate reads the tipjob roster on every return, but the project reads it only when s1a.tips is true, and the interview never asks it otherwise: the candidate requires answers the source does not need, since Part II is filled out only by someone who received qualified tips. Its value differences contradict the source. stage12.tips.no_valid_ssn gives $8,000.00 to a filer without a valid SSN (project $0.00). stage13.tips_spouse_no_ssn gives $0.00, because it counts the employer of the joint-return spouse without a valid SSN as a second employer (project $15,000.00, the SSN holder’s reported tips). stage13.tips_only_spouse_no_ssn gives $5,000.00 (project $0.00). The other value records are married filing separately returns, which s3.mfs refuses. One-employer tips themselves agree, because tipjob.col_d equals tipjob.amount within scope (column (c) refuses on s2.other). The project-unknown is a partial that withholds s1a.tips.
